lines.text: Speed the Earth up fast, and the oceans leave the poles.
lines.phonemes: spˈiːd ðɪ ˈɜːθ ˌʌp fˈæst, ænd ðɪ ˈoʊʃənz lˈiːv ðə pˈoʊlz.

lines.text: A spinning planet pushes water outward, toward the equator, exactly as it pushes you. Speed the spin up quickly and the ground cannot adjust in time. At a twelve hour day, the water wants to stand about thirty-three kilometers higher at the equator than at the poles, extra, compared with today. The whole ocean is only about three point seven kilometers deep. So the water does not simply rise. It drains toward a belt around the equator, while the poles dry out. This is a rough, first guess, but the direction is certain.
